# Ship Orbital Support Weapons
## Command: Arming the Ship Open the ship weapons arming terminal with command access. Choose [bold]at least one different weapon, up to the limit displayed by the terminal[/bold] and confirm. The default limit is two. [color=red]Confirmation permanently locks the entire loadout for the operation. Picking fewer than the limit does not leave slots available for later.[/color] All selected weapons share [bold]one pool of fire missions[/bold] shown by the terminal (two by default). Any armed weapon spends from that pool, and more terminals or batteries cannot reset it. Each ship has its own loadout, fire-mission pool, and cooldown. Decks in one ship's Z-level network share them; identical ships do not.
## Repairing the Batteries
The ship has orbital batteries, and either one can fire any mission. An anchored battery must be installed on your ship before command can arm weapons. [bold]Every shot burns out the battery that fires it.[/bold] Before it can fire again, work through its eight repair steps in order: - Crowbar: pry open the breech hatch. - Screwdriver: unscrew the coil housing. - Wrench: unbolt the burnt-out coil assembly. - Wirecutters: cut away the fused wiring. - Welder: weld the replacement rail seams. - Wrench: bolt the coil assembly back in. - Multitool: recalibrate the targeting relay. - Screwdriver: screw the housing shut. Examine a battery to see which step is next. With both batteries burnt out, nothing can fire until one is repaired. Tech tree purchases can clear extra fire missions for strikes the terminal didn't pick.
## Overwatch: Calling a Strike Use the existing orbital bombardment tab, enter ground coordinates, select an armed weapon, and confirm fire. With Walking Barrage selected, a direction picker also appears for its travel direction. The first impact arrives [bold]24 seconds after launch[/bold]. A shared [bold]60-second cooldown[/bold] starts when the ship accepts a launch. Nearby troops receive the launch warning, then [bold]one directional warning three seconds later[/bold] pointing from their position toward the target. A final-approach warning precedes impact. Rejected targets, burnt-out batteries, cooldown failures, and an empty fire-mission pool consume nothing. Accepted launches spend one shared mission and burn out the battery that fired. Protection changes can intercept later impacts without a refund. Once the ship has armed weapons, overwatch picks from its fire missions instead of the standard orbital cannon.
## Anti-Air Defense: IX-50 MGAD
The ship's IX-50 MGAD cannon is controlled from its system console, which needs command or engineering access and engineering training. Pick a [bold]defense zone[/bold] on the ship to protect, or clear targeting to leave every zone open. When a hijacked dropship heads for the protected zone, the MGAD fires on it and forces it to divert to a different zone. Everyone aboard the dropship feels the ship jostle and turn, and the defending faction is told which zone was saved partway through the flight. [bold]The MGAD only works once.[/bold] Any hijacked dropship heading for the ship knocks the system out, whether or not it was diverted. After that the console is disabled for the rest of the operation. The overwatch console shows the MGAD's status, its current zone, and whether it has engaged. Pick the zone you can least afford to lose, such as the hangar or engineering, and change it as the threat moves.
## Strike Profiles Scatter is the maximum distance between the requested target and an individual impact. Its blast radius extends beyond that point. - [bold]Gatling Barrage[/bold]: 120 small explosions, 0.15 seconds apart, scattered within 16 tiles. Each has a 1.5-tile blast radius. - [bold]Walking Barrage[/bold]: 9 HE explosions, one second apart, moving along a 16-tile line centered on the target. Each has a 6-tile blast radius. - [bold]120mm HE Barrage[/bold]: 12 explosions, 0.75 seconds apart, scattered within 16 tiles. Each has a 12-tile blast radius. - [bold]380mm HE Barrage[/bold]: 6 heavy explosions, 1.8 seconds apart, scattered within 6 tiles. Each has a 16-tile blast radius. - [bold]Airburst Strike[/bold]: 6 anti-personnel explosions, 0.8 seconds apart, scattered within 8 tiles. Each has a 12-tile blast radius, without breaking terrain tiles. - [bold]Precision Strike[/bold]: one 120mm-strength explosion at the exact target, with a 12-tile blast radius and no scatter. - [bold]Railcannon Strike[/bold]: devastating whole-body and structural damage in an exact 5x5 tile square, projected through [bold]every Z-level in the target's network[/bold]. Each level retains orbital-protection checks; unrelated maps are not hit. - [bold]Gas Strike[/bold]: a 30-tile-radius poison cloud lasting 30 seconds. Unprotected lungs and brains take 1 organ damage every 3 seconds, even after death. Xenos take no gas damage, but are slowed and their vision becomes hazy. Standard filters last 5 seconds of exposure; CBRN and WY filters last 15 seconds. Sealed internals also protect against the gas. - [bold]EMS Strike[/bold]: a 30-tile-radius field lasting 15 seconds. Everyone caught, including xenos and normally stun-immune targets, stays stunned until 25 seconds after the field disappears. Entering late or leaving early does not change that deadline. While inside, humans take 5 burn damage per second, up to 50 added damage per strike; xenos take the same damage without a cap. - [bold]Smoke Strike[/bold]: a non-damaging, opaque 30-tile-radius screen lasting 30 seconds.
[color=red]These expanded barrages can reach beyond the standard OB footprint. Keep friendly forces clear of both the scatter area and each shell's blast radius.[/color]
